question.leadin: Answer the following about Southeast Asian independence movements.
question.text: Ho Chi Minh led this nation's independence movement from France, which culminated in its victory at the Battle of Dien Bien Phu. The 1975 Fall of Saigon ended an American war in this country.
question.answerHtml: Vietnam [or Socialist Republic of Vietnam or Cong Hoa Xa Hoi Chu Nghia Viet Nam; prompt on SRV]
question.clue: Rioting against the presence of one of these countries in the other resulted in a coup which created the government in exile GRUNK.

swap.text: During the 1970s in this country, bordering Thailand and Vietnam, the Khmer Rouge under Pol Pot headed a genocide now referred to as the Killing Fields.
swap.clue: This country's Land Chenla kingdom developed into an imperial state under Jayavarman II.

question.leadin: There are many large rivers that start out in China or on the Chinese border, but are better known for being elsewhere. Name some of them.
question.text: It starts parallel to the Yangtze River on the Tibetan Plateau and flows south. It then continues through Laos and Cambodia until it cuts across Vietnam and has a delta at Ho Chi Minh City.
question.clue: This Southeast Asian river, rising in China's Qinghai Province and emptying into the South China Sea.

swap.leadin: This site, built by Khmer emperor Suryavarman II, was designed to resemble Mount Meru, the home of the gods in Hinduism.
swap.text: Name this temple complex near the city of Siem Reap, the largest religious structure in the world.
swap.clue: This structure unusually faces west unlike the Bayon to its north and is located near two barays.

question.leadin: Answer the following about immigration to Minnesota in recent history.
question.text: The fastest growing population of immigrants to Minnesota are the Karen people from this country. Rohingya Muslims in this country's Rakhine State are under persecution.
question.clue: A 16th century temple in this country noted for its sandstone blocks fitted together without mortar was built to commemorate a king's naval victory over Portugal.

swap.text: One of Raffles' most famous roles was his involvement in the conquest of this Indonesian island, which had previously been held by the Dutch East India Company. The colonial capital of Batavia was located on this island.
swap.clue: Islam was first introduced by the Wali Sanga, and its rulers of that faith included the Demak dynasty, which was founded by a citizen of the once-Hindu state of Majapahit.

question.leadin: Along with future vice president Mohamad Hatta, this leader declared his country's independence following the Japanese surrender in 1945 and he resisted Dutch re-colonization efforts.
question.text: Name this leader who aided in organizing the Bandung Conference, a precursor to the Non-Aligned Movement. This leader was a proponent of "Guided Democracy."
question.clue: This leader hosted the meeting which led to the formation of the Non-Aligned Movement in his country's city of Bandung.

swap.leadin: This man was captured by General Frederic Funston in the aftermath of the Battle of Tirad Pass.
swap.text: Name this revolutionary leader who was brought back to his country by Admiral George Dewey after the Battle of Manila Bay. This man was the first president of a country that would later gain independence due to the Tydings-McDuffie Act.
swap.clue: His followers killed potential rival General Antonio Luna to insure that he would lead them into such battles as the one at Tirad Pass.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the influence of Sanskrit culture pretty far away from India.
question.text: The past nine kings of this Southeast Asian country have used the name "Rama," after the mythical character. The British governess Anna Leonowens tutored one king of this nation.
question.clue: Since 1957, this country has criminalized insults against its monarchy under its lese-majeste laws.

swap.leadin: This man deposed Lon Nol, called himself "Brother Number One," and converted the Chao Ponhea Yat High School into Security Prison 21.
swap.text: Name this man who forced city residents, or "April 17 people," to work in the fields under horrific conditions.
swap.clue: Relations between this man's government and its Eastern neighbor deteriorated during his rule, leading to a Vietnamese invasion that ousted him from power.

question.leadin: Often compared to Donald Trump, this fan of death squads is nicknamed The Punisher.
question.text: Name this world leader who was formerly mayor of Davao City on the island of Mindanao.
question.clue: Pope Francis accepted an apology from this public figure for calling the pope a "son of a whore."

swap.leadin: This country's namesake Solidarity Convention formed in 1965 to oppose ethnic discrimination.
swap.text: Name this country, whose Constitution's Article 153 gives its native Bumiputera ("boo-mee-POO-teh-ruh") people preferred status. Race riots in 1969 forced the resignation of this country's first Prime Minister, Tunku Abdul Rahman.
swap.clue: In 1970, this country introduced policies to equalize its bumiputera peoples and wealthy Chinese minority.

question.text: Roel van Duyn, the founder of Provo, credits the offshoot group "Baastards" with leading the first Dutch protest against this conflict. Harold Wilson sent the Davies Mission to attempt to negotiate an end to this conflict.
question.clue: Students wearing black armbands to protest this war led to the case of Tinker v. Des Moines.

swap.text: General Harold Briggs approved the use of this chemical to destroy jungles during the Malayan Emergency. It was more famously used in the Vietnam War.
swap.clue: This carcinogen and defoliant that the United States used in an attempt to increase the visibility of Viet Cong troops.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the 30th of September Movement, whose most significant action, the murder of six generals, actually took place on October 1st, 1965.
question.text: The military blamed this political party for the murders, using the 30th of September Movement as a pretext for the mass murder of its members. This party was subsequently banned in March 1966, and remains illegal today.
question.clue: This party was exonerated of responsibility for a coup attempt in the "Cornell Paper" written by Benedict Anderson and Ruth McVey.

swap.leadin: Name the following places that were part of Dutch colonization in Southeast Asia.
swap.text: The Dutch East India Company captured this key trading city, located on a namesake strait, in 1641 in alliance with the Sultan of Johor. It became part of the Straits Settlements when it was ceded to the British, but is still home to a Dutch Stadhuys [stat-HOUSE], or city hall, with a distinctive red clock tower.
swap.clue: Control of this city hyperbolically afforded control over Venice according to the Suma Oriental of Tome Pires ("TOH-may PEE-rish"), who spent two years in this city after arriving from Goa.

question.leadin: Along with purchasing the superyacht Equanimity, funds embezzled in this scandal were ironically used to finance Red Granite Pictures's production of The Wolf of Wall Street.
question.text: Name this scandal in which president Najib Razak and his conspirators siphoned billions from Malaysia's sovereign wealth fund.

swap.leadin: A ruler from this family often held court with his pet orangutan Betsy, and he once held a trial in which he sentenced a man-eating crocodile to "be instantly killed without honours."
swap.text: Name this royal family, whose rule began when Omar Ali Saifuddin II granted its patriarch territory around the modern-day city of Kuching and the region of Bau. As rulers, they were known as the "White Rajahs."

question.leadin: This ruler of the Toungoo dynasty rose to the throne after his brother-in-law Tabinshwehti was assassinated.
question.text: Identify this king who ruled a unified Myanmar from 1551 to 1581, and was notable for his patronage of Buddhism, including the building of pagodas and the distribution of copies of the Tripitaka.

swap.leadin: The Rukunegara was instituted in part as a response to this event, which began as a reaction to the gains of the Gerakan and the Democratic Action Party, though ultimately the Alliance led by the UMNO was still in power.
swap.text: Name these 1969 race riots, which forced the government to respond with the New Economic Policy under its second national plan.
